description: Run by .github/workflows/renovate.yaml (self-hosted, as our own GitHub App). Nothing is automerged: a merge to main is a release (code) or a deploy (platform/, through Flux), so every update is a PR, checked by CI, merged by hand.

flux.description: HelmRelease chart versions, OCIRepository and GitRepository tags.

kubernetes.description: Container images in plain manifests (Authelia, hello).

customManagers.description: Versions with a `# renovate: datasource=... depName=...` comment on the line above, in workflows and in the sandbox's manifests (a chart value Renovate's flux manager doesn't read).
Tool versions in the sandbox image's Dockerfile: a `# renovate: datasource=... depName=...` comment on the line above an `ARG NAME=version`.
Container images pinned in the controller's Go code (the Postgres its databases run).
The same in Go code: the Paketo builder and pack image mcloud build uses (here and in run-deploy.yaml), the curl and Postgres images.

packageRules.description: Every update in one weekly PR: one review, one CI run, one deploy. The rules further down take back the updates that must not wait for it or be merged with others.
Providers and modules come from the OpenTofu registry, like `tofu init` (and the lock files) use.
kubectl must stay within one minor version of the cluster; minor bumps wait for a cluster upgrade.

The cluster's maxcloud controller (platform/clusters/personal/maxcloud.yaml) follows this repo's own controller/v* tags. The regex keeps Renovate off mcloud's v* tags, which it would otherwise read as newer versions of the same thing. Our own release: a PR as soon as there is one, no waiting period. release-please.yaml starts Renovate once the release's image is pushed.
Knative supports upgrading one minor version at a time: one PR per minor, merged in order, outside the weekly PR.
